messages.content: Write a concise investment research answer for the chat user, as the list of what it asserts. Reply with only a fenced block that opens with ```assertions on its own line, and nothing before or after it: a JSON array of at most 12 objects {"kind", "text", "evidence"}. The answer is rendered from this list alone, in its order: each figure, claim, period and company comes from the evidence an entry cites, and only an analyst_inference's text is shown as written. Every entry's text says it in one short sentence. Answer as a buy-side analyst would: first your takeaway, answering the question directly, as an analyst_inference; then the observations and comparisons that show the trend across every period shown, not just the latest, and what is strong or weak against the other periods or companies shown; an unknown_cause for a change the evidence gives no cause for; and last one specific counterpoint grounded in the data that cuts against the takeaway, as an analyst_inference. List nothing for what the data shown cannot tell: the answer's own notes say what is missing, from evidence_packet.gaps. If the data shown does not answer the question (the metric or period asked for is not there), list nothing about other figures in its place: reply with an empty list. Use only evidence_packet: never add facts, numbers, or events it does not hold. evidence_packet.figures are the figures you may cite, by id, each with its metric and, in a comparison, the company it belongs to. evidence_packet.claims are sourced statements you may cite, by id; evidence_packet.disagreements names claims that may conflict, and an inference never picks one side. If claims_status is unavailable, research claims could not be read, so never say there are none. Never state a cause the data does not show (a charge, supply constraints, heavy spending): a cause stated by management is a management_attribution citing its claim, and a change the evidence gives no cause for is an unknown_cause. kind is "observation" (what figures show; evidence lists their F ids only), "comparison" (a high or low, a ranking, or a trend of exactly one metric, so one comparison per metric; a segment breakdown is one metric, revenue, across segments; evidence lists the F ids of every company, segment or period it covers, and a comparison across periods cites every period shown for its metric; add "op" and "result": op "highest" or "lowest" with result the F id that is highest or lowest; op "order" with result an array of every F id it cites, highest first ({"kind":"comparison","text":"Revenue is highest at AAPL, then NVDA, then AMD.","evidence":["F1","F5","F9"],"op":"order","result":["F9","F1","F5"]}); or op "trend" with result one of "rose", "fell", "flat", "rose_throughout", "fell_throughout", "rebounded" or "pulled_back"), "management_attribution" (what a claim says management stated; evidence lists its C id), "unknown_cause" (a change the evidence gives no cause for; evidence lists the F id of each figure that changed), or "analyst_inference" (what the observations, comparisons and management attributions mean, in words, such as revenue concentrated in one segment; evidence may be omitted; add "supports": the array indexes of every observation, comparison and management_attribution whose content it uses (a figure, a price return, scale, a ranking, a charge management stated), and it says nothing those supports do not show, not even hedged ("may already be priced in"); add "subject": the company label the inference is about, one its evidence covers). An analyst_inference's text is words only: the figures are its supports', so it writes no digit, period label or packet id ("a year earlier", not FY2025). Never compute new figures such as growth rates, margins, differences, or ratios, and never state a magnitude in words ("roughly double", "six times", "larger than X's whole revenue"): say only the direction ("higher", "faster", "larger") without how much. When the answer covers more than one company, an analyst_inference's text names no company, not even in the counterpoint: who leads, trails, rose or fell is shown from the comparisons it rests on, so rest a ranking or direction on its comparison and say only what it means ("the margin lead funds more research", not "NVDA leads AMD"); the text refers to its subject as "it" or "its" ({"kind":"analyst_inference","subject":"AMD","text":"Its net margin may understate underlying profitability, given the one-time charge management disclosed.","supports":[2,3]}). When evidence_packet has neither figures nor claims, reply with an empty list.

You check the analyst inferences in a financial research answer. Each inference comes with what it rests on:
its supports (the observations, comparisons and management attributions it cites, each figure as the data
gives it, each claim as its source words it), the checked results of the comparisons among them, and its
subject, the company it is about. rest_of_answer is the answer's other checked observations and comparisons,
written the same way; the page may show one of them inside a comparison that states its figures.
figures_shown holds the figures the page's tables and charts show, a line per table, headed by its title when it
has one. companies lists every company the answer covers; rest_of_answer and figures_shown cover every one of
them, and an inference may rest on another company's figures when it compares them. Judge each inference
against its subject, checked results, supports, rest_of_answer and figures_shown; no outside knowledge, and
nothing from another inference. A company may be named by ticker, name or alias, in any case ("nvda",
"Nvidia", "Advanced Micro Devices"): naming one is fine, but what the inference says about it must be backed
like anything else. Qualitative words that summarise the figures (large, concentrated, higher, slowing) are
fine when the figures bear them out, and so is an exact count of the items the answer lists ("the two
companies", "four segments", "the eight quarters shown"). That covers no duration and no difference between
dates or values ("a one-month offset", "an eight-month gap"): those are amounts in words.

Answer two questions about each inference.

verdict: how it relates to what the answer shows. When both unsupported and contradicted apply, contradicted wins.
- entailed: its supports, the rest of the answer and the figures shown state or clearly imply what it says.
- unsupported: it contradicts nothing shown but claims something the answer neither states nor implies, such
  as a cause, a forecast, a trend, or a metric, segment or period not shown. A hedge does not make it
  supported: a valuation or market reading such as "may be priced in" or "the market may already reflect" is
  unsupported unless the answer shows it.
- contradicted: something it says disagrees with the figures or checked results shown: who leads, trails, is
  highest or lowest, or the order it states; a direction it states (rising, falling, expanding, recovering)
  against a checked trend or the figures; or any other statement the figures shown make false.

worded_amount, whatever its verdict: true when the inference's own words state any amount, fraction, multiple
or span of time, even when the figures bear it out: money, a percentage, a growth rate, a multiple or fraction
("doubled", "four times", "two-thirds"), or a duration or a difference between dates or values ("a
one-month offset", "an eight-month gap"), e.g. "hundreds of millions of dollars", "a quarter billion
dollars", "one and a half percent", "single-digit growth". An exact count of the items the answer lists
("the two companies", "four segments", "the eight quarters shown") is not one, and neither is a word that
names no quantity ("the gap", "the offset", "higher"), whatever the figures say. Otherwise false.

Reply with JSON only, one verdict per inference id; if you correct yourself, the last JSON in the reply is read:
{"verdicts":[{"id":<id>,"verdict":"entailed"|"unsupported"|"contradicted","worded_amount":true|false,"reason":"<one short sentence>"}]}
Give a reason for every verdict but entailed, and whenever worded_amount is true; otherwise leave it out.
